PullRequest.Title: editor: restore connected tab border and divider customizations
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Connected editor tabs still suppressed `tab.activeBorder` and gave `tab.border` conflicting paint ownership after the broader color-customization restoration in #337986. This restores the remaining legacy border customizations and separates rounded tab boundaries from inter-tab dividers.

- Restore active top, bottom, hover, selected, modified, focused, and unfocused border customizations in Connected tabs.
- Add `tab.divider`, which inherits `tab.border` by default but can be customized independently.
- Keep paint ownership style-specific:
  - Legacy continues using `tab.border` as its separator and renders no dedicated divider.
  - Pill uses rounded `tab.border` outlines plus dividers at every adjacent boundary.
  - Connected uses `tab.border` for the active document cap and dividers only between inactive neighbors.
  - High Contrast keeps complete theme-owned tab boundaries and renders no redundant divider.
- Keep rounded top and bottom accents inside Pill and wrapped Connected corners, and avoid duplicate first-tab/editor-frame edges.

Fixes #325250.

## Visuals

The issue contains the failing before state. These captures show the fixed implementation.

### Connected customization in native Code OSS

Dark Modern with distinct active/inactive surfaces, active top and bottom accents, a structural active-tab boundary, and dividers only between inactive neighbors:

![Native Code OSS with customized Connected tab boundaries, surfaces, accents, and inactive dividers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/0162cbe9-e5d8-450a-a29e-8072475a0257)

### Same tokens across tab styles

Top to bottom: Legacy keeps its existing separators without dedicated dividers; Pill uses rounded boundaries and dividers at every adjacency; Connected gives the active cap boundary ownership and limits dividers to inactive neighbors.

![Matched Legacy, Pill, and Connected production fixtures using the same custom colors](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/767e0d39-4e9d-4fbe-b350-eb0d8334f26d)

### Wrapped Connected tabs

An upper-row active tab remains a standalone pill. Its customized top and bottom accents stop before the rounded corners.

![Wrapped Connected tabs with inset top and bottom accents on the upper-row pill](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1575eff9-84a6-45fd-be52-5fb896adda45)

### High Contrast defaults

Top to bottom: Dark HC and Light HC with no color overrides. Complete theme-owned tab boundaries remain visible and no dedicated divider is added.

![Dark and Light High Contrast Connected tabs using complete stock boundaries without dedicated dividers](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d076758e-f98b-47e1-8a71-75bd85710540)

## Testing

1. Enable Modern UI and set `workbench.experimental.modernUIEditorTabStyle` to `connected`.
2. Customize `tab.border`, `tab.divider`, `tab.activeBorder`, and `tab.activeBorderTop` with distinct colors. Verify the active cap uses the tab boundary and top/bottom accents, while dividers appear only between adjacent inactive tabs.
3. Switch to `pill`. Verify each rounded tab uses `tab.border`, top and bottom accents stop before the corners, and dividers appear between every adjacent pair, including beside the active tab.
4. Disable Modern UI or use Legacy tabs. Verify the existing `tab.border` separator remains the only shared-edge paint and no dedicated divider is duplicated.
5. Wrap tabs onto multiple rows. Verify upper-row active tabs retain Pill geometry with inset accents and bottom-row active tabs remain connected to the editor.
6. Switch between Dark High Contrast and Light High Contrast without color overrides. Verify complete stock tab boundaries and active focus ownership remain visible, with no dedicated divider.
7. Exercise hover, modified, multi-selection, pinned, split-group, clipped, compact-height, and action-left states.

## Validation

- `npm install`
- `npm run compile`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- Modern UI and multi-editor tab unit suites
- Editor-tab production component fixture Playwright suite
- Stylelint for the changed tab styles
- Freshly built native Code OSS token audit across focused, hover, multi-selected, pinned, drag-and-drop, modified, and unfocused states

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, its unconditional reachability from doLayoutTabsWrapping, and the animation-frame layout call path are explicit. Repository-wide search shows production uses of first-in-row are confined to connectedEditorTabs.css, so the added work is unnecessary for legacy and pill bars. Exact milliseconds vary with tab count and host/browser speed, which is reflected in low severity.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread CPU and per-tab DOMTokenList operations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Two live-DOM class operations are added for every open tab in each editor group on every non-wrapping layout; cost grows linearly with tab count and with resize/layout event frequency after animation-frame coalescing.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased UI-thread layout/render latency and reduced resize frame throughput
Findings.PreviousBehavior: For the normal non-wrapping state, doLayoutTabsWrapping returned without scanning all tab children for row-boundary classes; it only removed last-in-row when transitioning out of wrapping.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every non-wrapping tab-bar layout now scans all tab DOM children and performs two DOMTokenList operations per tab, including default legacy and pill tab bars.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT lines 2316-2324 add an unconditional loop over every tab whenever tabs are not wrapping, invoking classList.toggle/remove for each child. Before this diff, the non-wrapping path had no row-boundary per-tab pass unless wrapping had just been disabled.
Findings.Title: Gate row-class updates to connected tab bars
Findings.Impact: With many open editors, resizing the window or editor groups, opening editors, or decoration/toolbar updates add O(number of tabs) synchronous DOM work on the UI thread per coalesced layout, increasing resize/render latency and risking dropped frames on large tab sets even in tab styles that do not use the class.
Findings.Evidence: MultiEditorTabsControl.layout schedules doLayout on the next animation frame; doLayoutTabs always calls doLayoutTabsWrapping. The new else branch at 2316 scans tabsContainer.children on every non-wrapping layout. Layout is triggered by group/window layout and explicitly by decoration and toolbar changes, and opening an editor redraws/layouts the control. Each iteration calls classList.toggle and classList.remove on live DOM. All production selectors consuming first-in-row are under .modern-ui-connected-editor-tabs in connectedEditorTabs.css; legacy and pill tabs cannot use this class.
Findings.Recommendation: Pass the already-computed connected-tab state into this helper and run the non-wrapping first-in-row assignment only for connected tabs (clearing it only when leaving that mode), rather than scanning every legacy and pill tab bar on every layout.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resize or update a non-wrapping editor tab bar
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Window/editor-group resize, editor open, decoration change, or toolbar-size change calls MultiEditorTabsControl.layout; the next animation frame synchronously runs doLayout -> doLayoutTabs -> doLayoutTabsWrapping before the frame can render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: All open tabs in every laid-out editor group; effective cardinality is one toggle/remove pair per tab per coalesced non-wrapping layout, with no deduplication inside the pass.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each tab control permits one pending animation-frame layout and folds newer options into it. Multiple visible editor groups can each run their own coalesced layout in the same frame; the per-group tab loops are serial on the UI thread.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache or remote data is involved. Tabs and divider nodes persist for the lifetime of each open tab; warm layouts reuse them. Row-boundary state is recomputed on every layout rather than cached, while the layout scheduler coalesces repeated requests within one animation frame.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added non-wrapping loop is directly on the animation-frame layout path and repository search establishes that first-in-row has no production consumer outside connected-tab CSS.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact added milliseconds depend on browser DOMTokenList cost, machine speed, editor-group count, and unusually large tab sets. The linear UI-thread mechanism is certain, but likely small for ordinary tab counts, so the finding is low severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable low-severity regression: the diff adds an unconditional O(tab count) live-DOM class pass to legacy and pill bars even though only connected CSS consumes first-in-row.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore editor tabs and render dividers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Opening/restoring editors synchronously constructs each tab, including the new divider element, before the tab bar is ready. Subsequent selection and hover changes are CSS style/repaint work and do not reconstruct the divider.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of open/restored editor tabs; one additional element per tab, released with the tab.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Tab creation is a serial DOM construction loop for newly opened editors. Bulk restoration creates one node per effective editor tab; no asynchronous concurrency or burst across an external service is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tab DOM is created once and reused until close. The new divider node is eagerly created once per tab and hidden by default for legacy/high-contrast styles; there is no separate cache, retry, or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that one retained DOM node is added per tab across all styles; low confidence that this bounded increment has a meaningful user-visible cost.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large restored workspaces can contain many tabs, but one simple hidden element per tab is bounded by the already-retained tab collection and is small relative to each tab's existing widget subtree.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the eager allocation is linear and broader than the styles that display it, but the bounded single-node increment does not independently establish a concrete performance regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply a theme or editor-tab color customization
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On theme or color-customization changes, the theming participant resolves colors, builds one declaration array, and injects one CSS rule before repaint. Normal tab interaction does not rerun the collector.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Fixed set of tab color identifiers per theme update; independent of tab count until the browser's normal style recalculation, which was already required for theme changes.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Theme participant execution is synchronous and serialized with the theme update. Color declarations are accumulated once, not per tab.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Theme colors are resolved from the in-memory ColorThemeData during theme participant execution. The refactor emits the same declarations plus two border/divider variables; there are no cold network reads, retries, or persistent caches.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed collector remains a single theming-participant call with a fixed number of in-memory operations.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The additional color lookups/string declarations are constant-sized and negligible compared with the existing theme-rule generation and global style recalculation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: no new external boundary, fan-out, cache failure, or collection-scaled serialization is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Hover, focus, or switch active connected/pill tabs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Pointer hover, focus, selection, and active-editor changes update existing classes, after which browser style matching and painting determine borders/dividers. The added adjacent-sibling selectors inspect only neighboring tabs.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible/open tabs in a group and frequency of hover/selection changes; adjacent divider ownership is local to each boundary.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Browser style and paint work is synchronous on the UI/rendering pipeline and naturally coalesced by frame rendering; no application-level parallelism exists.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: CSS selectors operate on the existing tab DOM; no application cache is involved. Browser style data is invalidated only by normal active/selected/hover/class changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that the diff adds style/repaint rules but no new scripted layout read on hover/selection.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Selector cost depends on DOM size and browser implementation, but selectors are scoped to editor tab containers and use local child/adjacent-sibling relationships, not unbounded descendant scans or forced geometry reads.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the additional CSS paint ownership and pseudo-elements do not prove forced layout, repeated reconstruction, or a meaningful new scaling cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 12 changed files and all diff pages. Traced tab creation, animation-frame layout, wrapping/non-wrapping row bookkeeping, theme-rule generation, and dynamic CSS paint paths. Submitted one low-severity synchronous UI-work finding for the unconditional per-tab non-wrapping class pass; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, network, or serialization boundaries are introduced or moved onto these scenarios.
